Summary

Updates the web extension data for Safari 27, corrects some older Safari entries, and adds impl_url links for unsupported features that have an open WebKit bug.

  • Safari 27: tabs.move() and windows.create() tabId (macOS only).
  • Safari 27.2: setAccessLevel() on every storage area, and scripting.ExecutionWorld, ISOLATED and MAIN exposed in the scripting namespace. Per #30817, the values are supported from 15.4, so those entries are partial until 27.2.
  • Corrections: commands.onChanged (macOS 26), initiatorDomains and excludedInitiatorDomains (18.4), tabs.create openInReaderMode (18), webNavigation parentFrameId, action.onClicked OnClickData (not passed), and extension.inIncognitoContext (content scripts only).

Test results and supporting details

Checked against the Safari release notes, the WebKit and Safari source, and the WebKit Bugzilla bugs. npm run lint -- webextensions passes.

items.content_html:
Firefox 160 makes the context parameter of exportKeyingMaterial() required and adds the required outputLength parameter, matching the spec in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2079306.

Firefox 155-159 implemented an earlier draft: context was optional and the output was fixed at 32 bytes.

What I've done is added a subfeature outputLength_parameter for the new parameter.

I've marked FF155-159 support as partial_implementation with a note that attempts to capture this. Note that it isn't "really" partial - it was correct (I think) at the point it was submitted. However its only been around for 5 releases so this feels a bit like a significant spec completion and hence grounds to indicate the first version as partial. Happy to remove that if you want.

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46281
items.title: Firefox 160: WebTransport.exportKeyingMaterial() outputLength parameter

Summary

Firefox 159 fixes a bug whereby previously, maxInStage limits (see GPUSupportedLimits) were adjusted to the values of maxPerStage limits, but those adjustments were not correctly reported in the device limits.

Those adjustments are now correctly reported. See https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2006720, particularly the comments from https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2006720#c26 onward.

This PR updates the 151 notes to be more accurate and adds an entry showing the problem was fixed in 159. It's a bit of a weird situation, and hard to understand, and I've tried my best based on the info I've been given.

Summary

  • Update Chrome support for break-before: avoid-page to Chrome 108.
  • Update Chrome support for break-after: avoid-page to Chrome 108, including its paged_context entry.

Additional details

  • Chrome 108 release notes document printing support for the avoid value of break-before, break-after, and break-inside as part of LayoutNG printing.
  • Chromium's LayoutNG printing test updates also confirm that break avoidance requested by break-before and break-after is supported.
  • Based on this evidence, Chrome's version_added value is updated to 108 for avoid-page under break-before and break-after, including the break-after paged_context entry.

Closes #15255

items.content_html:
Summary

Rename ids to remove the "at_" prefix from nested @page at-rules.

This was only recently introduced in #30612. I should have insisted on removing all prefixed ids in my review...

At-rules generally have no "at_" prefix. Not the general ones, but also not the nested ones (nesting happens in @page and in @font-feature-values). We should either have the prefix everywhere or nowhere. Since at-rules never had a prefix, I'm removing this newly introduced prefix.

Also, as of openwebdocs/mdn-bcd-collector#3477, the Collector can test support for at-rules and relies on consistent BCD paths.

Test results and supporting details

Data is the same. The linter reordered the data.

Related issues

#30612

Adds css.properties.outline-offset.inset for the inset keyword value of outline-offset, which draws the outline inside the element's border edge.

Browser support

  • Safari 27 (2026-09-14): first stable release
  • All other browsers: not yet shipped

Additional Details

  • WebKit commit a69b24040c7a, bug 317779, landed 2026-07-07
  • STP 249 release notes explicitly list "Added support for outline-offset: inset" (released 2026-07-29, after Safari 26.6 on 2026-07-27 — so 26.6 does not include it)
  • Spec tracking: CSSWG issue #13765 (css-ui-4 not yet updated; spec_url points to #outline-offset in the interim)
  • WPT: PR #60879

Related issue:

mdn/content#45043

Summary

Mirror Edge 79+ support from Chromium for legacy-only Edge statements, so Chrome's notes, partial implementation, and removals apply to Edge 79+. Built output is unchanged. Adds an internal mirror: false opt-out and marks 241 features for review.

Test results and supporting details

  • Unit suite passes (371 tests).
  • Built data is byte-identical to main.
  • Data changes are limited to "mirror": false markers: 254 statements across 241 features. Reviewers can list every opt-out by searching for the flag.
  • Continuous support stays a single statement. A second statement appears only where the Chromium-era data differs.

Related issues
